summary: For the New Brunswick ED-to-disposition calibration dossier, the most useful discoverable complementary source is AHRQ’s HCUPnet ED dashboard: queryable, downloadable aggregate ED utilization statistics for participating state datasets, including a state-level benchmark rather than RWJUH or Saint Peter’s facility-level wait-time distributions. HCUP’s underlying NJ SEDD is a stronger potential source for encounter-level arrival/disposition inputs but is distributed through the HCUP Central Distributor; it is not an open direct download and its availability/terms must be verified before acquisition. These sources can inform descriptive external ranges and case mix; neither supports local calibration or causal intervention claims. Discovery only; no data were acquired.

sources.title: HCUPnet Data Tools – Emergency Department Setting
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ), Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project
sources.geography: State and national statistics for participating HCUP jurisdictions; suitable for a New Jersey state benchmark where query filters permit, not facility-specific estimates for RWJUH CCN 310038 or Saint Peter’s CCN 310070.
sources.period: HCUP years available in the interactive dashboard; selected year range must be recorded at query time. Not verified as an untouched future holdout period.
sources.grain: Aggregated ED utilization statistics by selectable geography, year, and displayed measure; not patient-level or hospital-level encounter records.
useful_fields: ED visit disposition/category measures available in the dashboard
Patient or visit characteristics exposed by dashboard filters
observed_facts: AHRQ describes the tool as providing hospital inpatient and emergency department statistics and identifies NEDS, SEDD, and SID as contributing ED data sources.
The ED dashboard includes state-specific ED visits, including visits resulting in admission; AHRQ notes that ED patients admitted to hospital are represented in SID.
HCUPnet offers a downloadable spreadsheet of the selected visualization, but the opened page does not provide a static direct file URL.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Use the dashboard’s ED setting and state-specific views to query New Jersey and a recorded set of available years and measures; download its spreadsheet through the dashboard. Save query parameters, access date, and output metadata. Treat results as state-level external descriptive benchmarks. For local calibration, separately request a deidentified RWJUH/Saint Peter’s event extract with arrival, triage, rooming, decision, boarding, and departure timestamps plus disposition and covariates.
limitations: No facility-specific estimates or ED waiting-time distributions for the two named hospitals are established by this dashboard.
State ED statistics are hospital-state based; they do not identify the patient’s home county or these facilities.
Dashboard definitions, suppression, and available stratifications should be checked for each query; selected data were not downloaded or inspected here.
Aggregate rates cannot identify causal effects of staffing, triage, boarding, or other interventions.

sources.title: HCUP State Emergency Department Databases (SEDD) – overview and availability leads
sources.publisher: AHRQ, Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project
sources.geography: State-specific NJ emergency department discharge records; not a publicly queryable Middlesex County or named-hospital series unless the distributed file and permitted identifiers support that scope.
sources.period: Year-specific state releases; the SEDD visit-count index lists years 2006–2025 and uses NA when a state-year is unavailable. The exact current NJ release availability was not confirmed in the opened page.
sources.grain: Potentially ED visit/discharge record × selected fields in a licensed/distributed state file; not acquired. Verify facility identifiers, timestamp availability, linkage, and suppression in release-specific documentation.
useful_fields: Visit disposition and admission status (verify NJ release)
Facility identifiers, arrival/visit timing fields, and data-year coverage (must verify in NJ release documentation)
observed_facts: AHRQ describes SEDD as longitudinal state-specific ED databases in the HCUP family.
The official file-composition index enumerates visit counts by state and year, with NA indicating a state-year is unavailable.
HCUP sources distinguish SEDD ED visits not resulting in admission from SID records for ED visits resulting in admission; validate the release-specific definitions before combining records.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Check the current HCUP Central Distributor availability table for New Jersey SEDD years; obtain the NJ data dictionary and pricing/access terms before ordering. If institutional eligibility and terms allow, request only the smallest year slice needed for a state-level external distribution benchmark, inspect field definitions and facility coverage, and document the data-use restrictions. Do not describe it as open data or assume it contains operational timestamps.
limitations: The pages could not be opened reliably in this session for complete terms or current NJ year-by-year distributor availability; access classification and next steps require independent verification.
SEDD may exclude ED visits resulting in admission, which can bias ED-to-disposition distributions if used alone.
No direct downloadable NJ encounter file URL was verified; source discovery does not constitute acquisition.
Potential record-level variables, identifiers, granular timing, and eligibility to purchase/use must be checked against the exact release documentation and agreement.

sources.title: HCUP SEDD File Composition – number of visits by year
sources.publisher: AHRQ, Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project
sources.geography: State × year; includes availability and visit counts across participating jurisdictions. This is a coverage check, not Middlesex County or hospital-specific data.
sources.period: Index lists 2006–2025; individual cells may be unavailable and should be checked for NJ in the rendered table before scoping any request.
sources.grain: One row per state and one column per data year, with the number of visits in the corresponding Central Distributor SEDD file.
observed_facts: The page labels the table as visit counts for HCUP Central Distributor SEDD files and states that NA indicates a state-year is unavailable.
The index is a source-coverage aid and does not provide encounter outcomes or timing parameters.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Inspect the New Jersey row in the live table, record available years and counts in the proposed acquisition scope, then cross-check the same years in the current Central Distributor availability and release documentation before any request.
limitations: Counts alone do not provide patient-level or facility-level calibration parameters.
A year appearing in the index does not establish that a specific release is currently orderable or that its fields suit ED-to-disposition modeling.
The exact NJ row values were not established in the opened content returned here.

missing_inputs: A deidentified event-level RWJUH and Saint Peter’s ED extract with exact event-time definitions for arrival, triage, rooming, orders, disposition decision, boarding start/end, and departure; unit/shift staffing and bed availability; disposition; relevant non-identifying case-mix variables; and extract/release timestamps.
An untouched chronological validation window that was not used for fitting, with explicit handling of event time versus extract/release time and operational changes during the period.
Facility-specific, source-verified data dictionary and mapping for timestamps, dispositions, missingness, transfers, left-without-being-seen, and admission/boarding cohorts.
Independent clinical and operational review of the causal graph and intervention assumptions; public aggregate data cannot supply these assumptions.
Verified access, rights, retention, and permitted use terms for any HCUP SEDD release sought.
simulation_use: Use HCUPnet only as a state/national external descriptive benchmark for broad ED utilization and disposition proportions after recording the exact query and period. Use SEDD only if access and release fields are verified, as an external encounter-level distribution benchmark with the admission-record limitation addressed. Do not calibrate named-hospital arrival, service, boarding, or disposition parameters from CMS snapshots or these aggregates. Build a directed causal graph before intervention scenarios (e.g., arrivals/case mix and staffing/bed state affect queues and service; disposition needs and inpatient capacity affect boarding and departure); label graph edges and intervention assumptions as hypotheses until institutional evidence validates them. Split fitting and untouched chronological holdout by event time, freeze the model before evaluation, and report prediction error and sensitivity ranges by outcome and stratum. Keep conservation/replay checks (flow counts, timestamp ordering, capacity constraints, reproducible seed) separate from clinical/human validation (domain-owner review and comparison with withheld real outcomes).
limitations: This is a bounded public-source discovery exercise; no dataset was downloaded or acquired.
HCUPnet provides aggregate state/national measures and cannot calibrate hospital-specific joint distributions or establish causal effects.
The opened HCUP SEDD overview and NJ file-composition search leads returned internal errors when opened; their details and applicable rights/access terms remain unverified.
No local Middlesex County facility-level operational dataset was identified within the two-search/four-open budget.
No calibrated claim is made; all parameter values and causal relationships require independent institutional data and domain-owner review.
